messages:
tasha: Hey all, day 2 and flagged down by a manager — they asked me about secrets rotation for a PoC I set up. I want to summarize the minimum safe plan. Who should I loop in and what steps are required?

ben: welcome! quick summary: non-prod PoC -> short-lived Vault token; staging -> service account with rotation; prod -> rotation policy + SRE + security signoff.

infra-bot: Note: For non-prod tokens use `secrets-cli request --env dev --ttl 2h`. For staging, request a service identity (REQ-XXXX) that enters our rotation pipeline (30d default).

security: hi @tasha — important distinctions: rotate whenever creds escape (accidental paste), before onboarding external vendors, before promoting to prod. We require an incident-style rotation ticket for suspected compromises.

tasha: if I promote a PoC to run nightly in staging, what changes?

oncall-sre: scheduled jobs must run under a service identity (not a human token). Open a ticket to provision the identity and we’ll add it to automated rotation and monitoring. Owner oncall + infra handle the rotation schedule.

ben: rotation checklist (short): 1) create service identity 2) add to rotation pipeline (auto-schedule) 3) update consumers and verify 4) revoke old creds and run smoke tests 5) close rotation ticket with audit log links.

security: Also add a versioned secret in Vault (use metadata) so you can rollback. Audit logs are mandatory for prod/staging rotations. We’ll help validate the audit traces.

tasha: who signs off on the rotation? manager + SRE?

oncall-sre: manager ack + SRE co-sign for staging; for prod add security approver. Use the Secrets Portal and include the new secret path, estimated downtime (usually none), and testing plan.

infra-bot: Portal: https://company.internal/secrets. Use category "rotation" and include `old_secret_version` and `new_secret_version` fields. Tickets auto-assign to service owner and infra oncall.

tasha: say I accidentally pasted a token into a public gist — what's the emergency flow?

security: immediate steps: 1) revoke token via `vault token revoke <token>` 2) open a rotation incident (INC-...) and set priority P0 if public leak 3) rotate secret, update consumers 4) notify legal/security if leak is external. We’ll run an audit and suspend any downstream integrations until validated.

ben: pro tip: use `secrets share --ephemeral` for demos instead of long-lived tokens, and never paste tokens in channels. Also enable `vault-agent` templating for local apps to avoid env var leakage.

devex-bot: New-hire tip: quick walkthrough slides on rotation best practices are in the handbook: https://company.internal/devex/secrets-onboarding (15min). Book a session with @ben if you want a live walkthrough.

tasha: great, I'll book a 15m with @ben and file the ticket for a staging service id if I promote the job. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
